articles.title: How to Evaluate a Los Angeles Neighborhood for a Restaurant
articles.intent: How should an operator evaluate a Los Angeles restaurant neighborhood?
articles.rationale: Replaced unsupported best-area rankings with concept requirements, address-level observation, occupancy costs and jurisdiction checks. Preserved six neighborhood groupings as investigation examples rather than forecasts or demand claims.

articles.title: Restaurant Due Diligence Findings: Proceed, Renegotiate or Pause?
articles.intent: How should a restaurant buyer assess due diligence findings?
articles.rationale: Rebuilt the overlapping checklist as findings interpretation: evidence gaps, financial discrepancies, lease and approval risk, equipment and health issues, issue log, specialist escalation and proceed/renegotiate/pause decisions. Prominently links to the primary Help checklist.

articles.title: Restaurant Valuation in Los Angeles: Earnings, Assets & Risk
articles.intent: How is a Los Angeles restaurant valued?
articles.rationale: Distinguishes operating business from asset transaction; explains documented earnings, supported SDE adjustments, replacement labor, lease continuity, equipment, approvals, location risk and asking price versus transaction economics. Removed universal multiple and expiry claims; labeled the earnings arithmetic hypothetical.

articles.title: What Is a Second-Generation Restaurant Space?
articles.intent: What is a second-generation restaurant space?
articles.rationale: Preserved the infrastructure investigation; added system-by-system evidence, ownership and lease obligations, approvals versus prior use, ADA and health jurisdiction. Replaced promised six-figure savings with a complete cost comparison.

articles.title: Type 41 vs. Type 47: California Restaurant Liquor Licenses
articles.intent: What is the difference between California Type 41 and Type 47?
articles.rationale: Added a privileges comparison and food-service context; separated ABC from local land-use approval, explained transfer/new-license considerations, and replaced price/availability promises with cost components and official fee links.

articles.title: How to Buy a Restaurant in Los Angeles
articles.intent: How do I buy a restaurant in Los Angeles?
articles.rationale: Preserved acquisition breadth: structure, budget, search, offer, diligence, lease, ABC/health, escrow, closing and transition. Removed formula prices, financing percentages and timelines. Added links to relevant guides, listings and specialist services.

articles.title: Restaurant Due Diligence Checklist
articles.intent: What belongs in a restaurant due diligence checklist?
articles.rationale: Designated the primary checklist; retained detailed financial, lease, ABC, health, building/accessibility, equipment, contract and staffing review. Clarified the evidence and contractual limits, added an issue log and a link to the distinct Blog findings guide.

articles.title: How to Sell a Restaurant in Los Angeles
articles.intent: How do I sell a restaurant in Los Angeles?
articles.rationale: Preserved preparation, valuation, confidentiality, buyer qualification, negotiation, diligence, lease, licensing, escrow and transition. Removed universal discounts, multiples and timing; replaced absolute confidentiality and employee/tax directions with transaction-specific review.

articles.title: How a California ABC Restaurant License Transfer Works
articles.intent: How does a California ABC restaurant license transfer work?
articles.rationale: Owns procedure: transfer routes, application package, premises approval, escrow coordination, conditional temporary permits, license conditions, local authorization and cost/timing dependencies. Cross-links the license-type comparison; removes automatic-operation and fixed-timeline claims.

articles.title: Restaurant Lease Assignment Guide for Los Angeles Transactions
articles.intent: How does a restaurant lease assignment work?
articles.rationale: Distinguishes assignment, sublease and new lease; covers consent clauses, landlord package, options, guaranty structures, rent relief and sale coordination. Qualifies the California consent standard, release and abatement; removes fee/time averages. Primary parent is now restaurant leasing.

articles.title: Beverly Hills Restaurant Transactions: Location, Lease & Approvals
articles.intent: What local issues matter in a Beverly Hills restaurant transaction?
articles.rationale: Reframes a broker-intent page as local transaction education: city jurisdiction, zoning, occupancy terms, documented costs, business certificate, outdoor dining, ABC and buyer/seller preparation. Preserves useful corridor examples while removing rent/premium and exclusivity claims.
